::: {.callout-note}
## Sample Reading Note

This is a format demonstration. It does not describe a specific publication or claim that FengLab has adopted a particular interpretation.
:::

## Why this paper belongs in the notebook

Begin with two or three sentences explaining why the paper matters to the lab’s scientific questions. Focus on the conceptual contribution rather than reproducing the abstract.

## What changed in our thinking?

Useful reading notes can distinguish among:

- a new biological observation;
- a method that changes what can be measured;
- a conceptual model that reorganizes existing evidence;
- a result that challenges an assumption; and
- an unresolved limitation that suggests a new experiment.

## Questions to carry forward

Conclude with a small number of questions that connect the paper to future work. When a real paper is discussed, include its complete citation and a direct link to the publication.

## Suggested citation block

**Paper:** Author list. “Article title.” *Journal* (Year).  
**Why we saved it:** One sentence in the lab’s own words.  
**Questions:** Two or three specific questions for discussion.
